subject.title: Custom cross-control selection engine so the whole chat transcript is drag-selectable

question: Should the Windows native chat own a custom cross-control selection and UI Automation subsystem, and if so should its first supported boundary be one message or the entire transcript?
rationale: The approach is technically plausible but creates a permanent interaction, accessibility, rendering, and performance contract whose scope and maintenance cost require explicit product ownership.

options.title: Prototype per-message selection
options.body: Sponsor a narrow spike crossing styled islands within one message and require keyboard, clipboard, UIA, rerender, scrolling, and visual proof before expansion.

options.title: Keep native controls
options.body: Retain native per-control selection plus the whole-message Copy affordance and avoid owning a parallel text-selection stack.

options.title: Build transcript-wide selection
options.body: Treat the logical transcript, multi-message selection, custom painting, and UIA provider as a larger planned native-chat initiative.

recommendation.title: Prototype per-message selection
recommendation.body: Sponsor a narrow spike crossing styled islands within one message and require keyboard, clipboard, UIA, rerender, scrolling, and visual proof before expansion.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice concerns native-app product scope and long-term ownership rather than a mechanical renderer repair.
